description: §14.8.9 declassification is VALUE-scoped, so it cannot suppress a gate at a sink the compiler refuses to mediate. Wrapping the protected row in u.reveal("passwordHash") at a RAW egress (a manual `new Response(...)`) does NOT suppress E-PROTECT-004 — the raw-egress gate is a floor with no exit. Re-authored at S352 from `protect-reveal-suppresses-e004`, which asserted the inverse (dpa-033 D3: a green test pinning a leak). Its sibling `protect-reveal-client-visible-runtime` is the contrast case: at a COMPILER-EMITTED sink, reveal does admit the named column.
rationale: §14.8.9 scopes declassification to the VALUE in four phrases: a protected-origin column reaches the client iff it is 'explicitly declassified via the field-level `reveal` construct AT THE VALUE' (SPEC.md:8506-8507); reveal 'stamps the named column's provenance descriptor as DECLASSIFIED-AT-THIS-VALUE' and 'the serializer admits a protected-origin column ONLY when its descriptor bears a `reveal` stamp AT THE SINK' (SPEC.md:8511-8513); the worked example is commented 'here only' (SPEC.md:8509). A raw egress is precisely a sink the compiler cannot introspect, so it cannot check the stamp — and the closed-world precondition at SPEC.md:8518-8524 mandates an unconditional SHALL fail closed there, naming no reveal exception. The prior body-wide suppressor was therefore the NON-CONFORMANT state: a `.reveal()` on a DIFFERENT query's row silenced the gate for the actually-returned, never-revealed row. Deleting it is conformance restoration, not an amendment. The value-scoped exit at a mediatable raw sink is dpa-033 (d), a separate later arc. provenance: ruling:user-voice-scrml.md S352 (dpa-033 (c)).
